items.title: Nifty weekly outlook: Nifty trapped in 23,900-24,750 range; fresh buying should remain selective
items.description: Nifty ended the week lower after consolidating in a narrow range, with the broader technical structure remaining unchanged. The index moved between 24,076.85 and 24,378.60, while India VIX declined 4.64% to 10.68. Support remains at 23,900–24,000, while a cluster of moving averages continues to cap upside in the 24,400–24,750 zone.

items.title: 10 penny stocks zoom up to 119% in just 2 months, 4 turn multibaggers. Did you own any?
items.description: Over the past two months, 10 penny stocks delivered gains ranging from 13% to 119%, with four emerging as multibaggers. The stocks were identified using a screen based on three key filters: a market capitalisation of less than Rs 1,000 crore, a share price below Rs 20 and a minimum latest trading volume of 5 lakh shares.The screen highlights low-priced, actively traded micro-cap stocks that have shown strong upward momentum. Penny stocks often attract investors with their low price points and potential for outsized returns, but they also carry substantial risks, including low liquidity, sharp volatility and limited transparency. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: FPIs turn buyers for second straight month, invest Rs 30,919 cr in August
items.description: During August, foreign portfolio investors added over Rs 30,000 crore to Indian equities, showcasing the ongoing trend of substantial market inflows for the second month in a row. This surge can be attributed to enhancing corporate earnings and a stable economic environment. Furthermore, easing global geopolitical tensions have aided investor optimism, yet uncertainties surrounding crude oil prices and US bond yields remain pressing issues.

items.title: 7 of top 10 firms shed Rs 1.13 lakh cr in m-cap; Airtel, Reliance worst hit
items.description: Last week observed a notable decline in market valuations, with seven out of the ten top firms witnessing a reduction of Rs 1.13 lakh crore. The greatest impact was felt by Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries, linked to concerns over global interest rates and geopolitical instability. Nonetheless, there was robust buying in IT stocks, which facilitated a recovery in the market on Friday.

items.title: Corporate actions this week: NTPC, Coal India among nearly 90 cos set to hit record dates for dividend payouts, bonus issues & stock splits
items.description: Nearly 90 companies, including NTPC, Coal India and Oil India, have scheduled record dates for dividends, bonus issues and stock splits from August 31 to September 4. Investors must hold the respective shares as of the record date to qualify. Mastek, Glenmark Pharma and Triveni Engineering are among Monday’s stocks, with several companies announcing dividends for shareholders.

items.title: Reliance Jio IPO: Google, Meta among 6 investors to retain stakes in Rs 37,700 crore offer
items.description: Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital arm Jio Platforms has secured Sebi approval for its IPO, taking one of India’s most closely watched listings a step closer to the market. The offering is expected to raise around Rs 37,700 crore and value the digital services company at nearly Rs 9.5 lakh crore, potentially making it one of the largest public offerings in India. The IPO will also see several marquee global investors retain their stakes in Jio Platforms. Here’s a look at the company’s key shareholders and their holdings:

items.title: GDP data, crude prices among 7 factors likely to steer D-Street this week
items.description: Indian equities are likely to take cues from a slew of domestic and global factors this week, including India’s first-quarter GDP data, US jobs numbers, crude oil prices, institutional flows and global technology sentiment. Analysts expect the Nifty to remain in consolidation, with the technical setup balanced as investors track key resistance and support levels.

items.title: When volatility rises, will you panic or buy? Depends on the watchlist you build now: 5 large-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 32%
items.description: Another worry has emerged for the markets, and it will drive the narrative in the short term. As usual, it comes from the US. The US Fed has signalled it may raise interest rates to keep prices under control. President Trump has, however, been loudly demanding lower rates, especially with elections coming up and ordinary Americans feeling the pinch of higher prices. So, there is now a tug of war at the very top of the world's most important economy, between a central bank worried about inflation and a government that wants cheaper money.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday
items.description: Indian equities rebounded on Friday, with strong gains in heavyweight IT stocks lifting the Sensex and Nifty after two consecutive sessions of losses. Analysts expect range-bound trading amid mixed global cues and geopolitical tensions, while Nifty faces resistance near 24,200 and support around 23,900.

items.title: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya seeks SEBI probe into sharp Sensex swing during CAS
items.description: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya has urged SEBI to investigate the sharp swings in the Sensex during the Closing Auction Session on August 27, when the index plunged over 2,000 points within minutes before recovering much of the loss. He questioned whether the new CAS mechanism, introduced on August 3, has weaknesses related to liquidity and price discovery.

items.title: Nifty mega caps are going nowhere. Why Samco CIO Umesh Mehta put 75% of his Flexicap fund beyond largecaps
items.description: Mutual Fund CIO Umesh Mehta says Nifty mega caps may remain subdued as institutional ownership limits fresh buying and earnings momentum shifts towards mid- and small-cap stocks. He explains why Samco Flexicap Fund has allocated 70–75% of its portfolio beyond large caps, while highlighting opportunities in defence, power, AI ancillaries and gold, and warning about IPO-led liquidity pressures.

items.title: MSCI rebalancing on Monday: Adani Energy, Groww set for big inflows; RIL, Jio Financial may face outflows
items.description: MSCI’s latest rebalancing is set to drive heightened trading activity in several Indian stocks on Monday, with revised weights taking effect from September 1. The final 30 minutes of Monday’s session could see significant activity as investors adjust positions. According to Nuvama Alternative and Quantitative Research, the changes include index additions and exclusions, along with weight revisions across several stocks.

items.title: SBI, SBI Capital Markets plan 1% NSE stake sale via IPO: Bank Chairman C S Setty
items.description: State Bank of India plans to divest nearly one percent of its National Stock Exchange stake.  This divestment will occur as part of the exchange's upcoming initial public offering.  SBI's mortgage portfolio is projected to surpass ten lakh crore rupees this quarter.  The bank holds a significant market share in the home loan segment.  Home loans are considered vital for India's overall economic growth.
